sentences: The directed Longest Detour problem asks whether a simple path from s to t exceeds the shortest-path distance by at least k edges.
Even the first nontrivial case asks whether any s-to-t path is longer than a shortest one.
The source leaves the polynomial-time versus NP-hard classification unresolved for this case on general directed graphs.
Its positive results for planar directed graphs do not settle the unrestricted problem.
Resolving the k=1 case would determine whether a seemingly tiny deviation from shortest paths already introduces the complexity associated with finding long simple paths.
